<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table
of Contents</a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of our internal investigation related
to potential FCPA violations, we suspended shipments to affected countries
while we put additional safeguards in place.&#160;
We also terminated several consultants and suspended relations with or
terminated some distributors in countries under investigation as circumstances
warranted.&#160; These actions resulted in a
decline in revenue from these countries during 2009.&#160; We resumed shipments to several countries
during the fourth quarter of 2009 and intend to resume shipments with new
safeguards or reallocate product to other countries during 2010.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Cost of
Goods Sold and Gross Profit</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our gross profit was $632.1 million and $492.1
million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 and December&nbsp;31, 2008,
respectively, representing gross margin of 41.2% and 35.8%, respectively.&#160; In general, our gross margin and cost of
goods sold are impacted by the volume and pricing of our finished products, our
raw material costs, production mix, yield, and cycle times, as well as our
production capacities and normal production shut-downs, and the timing and
amount of release of finished product.&#160;
The net impact of these items resulted in higher gross margin during the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 as compared to the prior year.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our cost of goods sold was $901.1 million, or 58.8%
of net revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, as compared to
$882.2 million, or 64.2% of net revenue, for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008.&#160; The decrease in our cost of goods
sold as a percentage of net revenue during 2009 was primarily attributable to
lower TPR unabsorbed infrastructure and start-up costs of $54.5 million and
lower inventory impairment provisions of $5.0 million.&#160; The beneficial effects of the foregoing were
offset by higher costs of production and costs associated with an increase in
production volumes, which aggregated $78.4 million.&#160; Due to the relatively fixed nature of our
factory overhead and certain other production costs, we experienced operating
leverage as production increased during 2009.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our cost of goods sold
for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 includes higher costs of production
of $14.7 million, including foreign exchange, and higher costs associated with
an increase in volumes of $52.8 million.&#160;
The impact of foreign exchange in our cost of production for the year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 is not material. During 2009, we incurred non-capitalizable
project and start-up costs of $36.9 million, an increase of $10.9 million, as
compared to the prior year, related to capital projects. The largest
component of our cost of goods sold is the cost of source plasma, which
represented greater than 50% of our cost of goods sold in 2009 and 2008. The
overall cost of source plasma is impacted by the fully-loaded collection cost
per liter, including donor fees, labor, soft goods, facility costs, testing and
unabsorbed TPR infrastructure and start-up costs, the cost of plasma purchased
from third-parties and variability in protein yields, among other factors. Our
internal cost per liter of plasma, including unabsorbed TPR infrastructure and
start-up costs, declined by 21.4% during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009,
primarily driven by lower unabsorbed infrastructure and start-up costs. Our
acquisition cost of plasma per liter of third party plasma increased slightly
by 0.30% during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 as compared to the year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2008. We fractionated approximately 3.6 million liters
of plasma during 2009, of which approximately 62% came from plasma collection
centers we own and approximately 38% came from third-party plasma supply
contracts.&#160; Due to our long manufacturing
cycle times, which range from 100&nbsp;days to in excess of 400&nbsp;days, the
cost of plasma is not expensed through cost of goods sold until a significant
period of time subsequent to its acquisition.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Unabsorbed TPR infrastructure and start-up costs
amounted to $44.0 million and $98.5 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2009 and 2008, respectively, representing approximately 2.9% and 7.2%,
respectively, of our net revenue.&#160; Our
cost of goods sold during 2009 benefited from lower unabsorbed TPR
infrastructure and start-up costs, which resulted from higher plasma volumes
collected at our plasma collection centers and improved labor efficiencies as
well as lower consulting and management support costs.&#160; Unabsorbed TPR infrastructure and start-up
costs during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 were negatively impacted by
costs associated with remediation efforts at certain plasma collection centers.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our inventory impairment provisions, net of
recoveries, decreased $5.0 million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009
as compared to the prior year.&#160; During the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, we recorded a net provision of $5.8 million
due to the plasma center cGMP issue described in </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#147;Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial
Condition and Results of Operations&#151;Matters Affecting Comparability&#151;Plasma
Center cGMP issue.&#148;&#160; During the year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, we recorded recoveries of $1.9 million related to
this issue.&#160; During the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2009 and 2008, we recorded net recoveries of $0.8 million and $7.1 million
related to a 2007 customer settlement as described in &#147;Management&#146;s Discussion
and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#151;Matters Affecting
Comparability&#151;Customer Settlement.&#148;&#160;
During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, we recorded an impairment
charge of $3.6 million primarily within cost of goods sold related to capital
lease assets and leasehold improvements at certain of our plasma collection
centers which were closed or were under development and we no longer plan to
open.&#160; During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, we also recorded a loss of $3.4 million within cost of goods sold related
to two lease commitments associated with properties that we no longer plan to
operate as plasma collection centers.&#160;
During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, we experienced a delay in
the restart of our manufacturing facility located in Melville, New York,
following a scheduled maintenance shut-down, which resulted in an inventory
impairment provision of $3.4 million.&#160; In
addition, during 2009, we recorded provisions of $4.2 million related to
short-dated finished goods inventories.&#160;
During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, we experienced lower
work-in-process inventory impairment provisions of $6.9 million as compared to
the prior year.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

infrastructure and start-up costs to decrease substantially in 2010, primarily
due to increased collections as well as cost reductions. This benefit will be
partially offset by increased cost of goods sold due to yield variability, less
efficient utilization of each incremental liter of plasma fractionated as we

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Operating

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our SG&amp;A was $289.9 million and $227.5 million
for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008, respectively, representing
an increase of $62.4 million, or 27.4%.&#160;
As a percentage of net revenue, SG&amp;A was 18.9% and 16.6% for the
years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160; Our share-based compensation expense recorded
in SG&amp;A increased $7.2 million during 2009 as compared to the prior year, driven
primarily by the acceleration of the vesting of certain of our Chairman and
Chief Executive Officer&#146;s stock options.&#160;
Our SG&amp;A included legal expenses of $6.0 million and $8.3 million
and retention expenses, excluding fringe benefits, of $5.0 million and $3.0
million related to our terminated merger agreement with CSL for the years ended
December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008 respectively.&#160;
Our SG&amp;A for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 was negatively
impacted by $8.0 million of legal costs associated with our internal
investigation into potential violations of the FCPA. </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We experienced higher sales and marketing
expenses during 2009 as a result of costs associated with our Gamunex CIDP
indication, Prolastin patient identification, as well as support for other products.&#160; We also experienced higher charitable
donations of $14.9 million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 as
compared to the prior year.&#160; Our
provision for uncollectible receivables and advances was $2.1 million higher
during 2008 as compared to 2009 as a result of non-cash charges related to
outstanding notes receivable and other advances made to one of our plasma
suppliers due to uncertainty regarding collection.&#160; In order to grow revenues through leveraging
our Gamunex brand and our CIDP indication, as well as our focus on A1PI patient
identification, we began a significant expansion in the size of our U.S. sales
force in the third quarter of 2009.&#160; We
are also increasing our sales and marketing organization in Europe as well as
in other international regions. We expect the sales force expansion to result
in an annual increase in SG&amp;A of approximately $10.0 million.&#160; Additionally, we expect that our share-based
compensation expense will decline subsequent to the first quarter of 2010 when
substantially all grants and awards under our 2005 Stock Option and Incentive
Plan, our 2006 Restricted Stock Plan and our Special Recognition Bonus Plan are
fully vested. Additional information regarding certain items impacting the
comparability of our results of operations is included in &#147;Management&#146;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of
Operations&#151;Matters Affecting Comparability.&#148;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our R&amp;D was $71.2
million and $66.0 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008,
respectively, representing an increase of $5.2 million, or 7.9%.&#160; As a percentage of net revenue, R&amp;D was
4.6% and 4.8% for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008,
respectively.&#160; R&amp;D expenses are
influenced by the timing of in-process projects and the nature and extent of
expenses associated with these projects.&#160;
The increase in R&amp;D year over year is primarily attributable to
increased spending during 2009 related to our Plasmin and recombinant Plasmin
new product candidates, partially offset by lower spending attributable to our
Prolastin-C A1PI and Gamunex subcutaneous administration life cycle management
projects.&#160; Additional information
regarding our R&amp;D projects is included in &#147;Management&#146;s Discussion and
Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#151;Research and
Development&#148; and &#147;Business&#151;Research and Development.&#148;&#160; We anticipate that R&amp;D will increase in
subsequent periods primarily as a result of increased Plasmin clinical trials
related to aPAO and ischemic stroke as well as increased spending related to
our development of recombinant A1PI and Factor VIII.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Total
Other Non-Operating Expense, net</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our other non-operating
expense, net, includes interest expense related to our indebtedness, which
amounted to $56.9 million and $85.7 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160; The
weighted average annualized interest rates on our outstanding indebtedness,
excluding amortization of deferred debt issuance costs and debt discount, were
3.4% and 7.2% for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008,
respectively.&#160; The benefit of the lower
cost of borrowings during 2009 was partially mitigated by higher interest
expense of $3.9 million related to our interest rate swaps as compared to 2008,
as a result of falling three-month LIBOR as compared to our fixed interest rate
swaps.&#160; The interest rate swap contracts
were settled and terminated as discussed below.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our product net revenue
was $1,334.6&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 as compared
to $1,196.7&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007,
representing an increase of $137.9&nbsp;million, or 11.5%. The increase
consisted of improved pricing of $122.3&nbsp;million, including foreign
exchange benefit of $9.7&nbsp;million, as well as volume increases of
$15.6&nbsp;million. Our other net revenue increased $17.9&nbsp;million
primarily due to increased royalties and licensing fees under collaborative
agreements, milestones, and other third party contract servicing agreements at
our Melville, New York facility.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

increase in our Gamunex product net revenue consisted of improved pricing of
$55.0&nbsp;million, including foreign exchange benefit of $1.8&nbsp;million,
partially offset by volume decreases of $24.0&nbsp;million. The higher Gamunex
pricing primarily related to U.S. and Canadian sales. We experienced lower
Gamunex volumes of $35.4&nbsp;million and $7.7&nbsp;million in the U.S. and </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Europe, respectively, which were partially offset by
higher Gamunex volumes of $13.0&nbsp;million and $6.1&nbsp;million in Canada
and other international regions, respectively. We continue to experience strong
demand for Gamunex globally. Our ability to meet this demand is dependent upon
our ability to secure adequate quantities of plasma and our ability to release
finished product into our distribution channels.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The $40.0&nbsp;million
increase in our Prolastin&nbsp;product net revenue consisted of improved
pricing of $19.0&nbsp;million, including foreign exchange benefit of
$7.6&nbsp;million, and higher volumes of $21.0&nbsp;million. The improved
Prolastin&nbsp;pricing was largely in Europe and the U.S., which increased
$10.5&nbsp;million and $7.6&nbsp;million, respectively. Prolastin&nbsp;volumes
improved $12.8&nbsp;million and $8.2&nbsp;million in the U.S. and Europe,
respectively. Increases in Prolastin&nbsp;volumes are largely a function of our
ability to identify and enroll new patients compared to the number of patients
lost due to attrition and competition. Our European growth will also depend
upon our ability to obtain appropriate reimbursement on a country by country
basis.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Fraction V product
category consists of albumin and Plasmanate, with albumin representing the
majority of sales in the category.&#160; The
$7.7&nbsp;million decrease in our Fraction V product net revenue consisted of volume
decreases of $17.0&nbsp;million, partially offset by improved pricing of
$9.3&nbsp;million. The albumin pricing increase was predominantly driven by
sales in the U.S., which contributed $7.7&nbsp;million to the overall pricing
improvement. Albumin volumes were negatively impacted by a change in production
mix during 2008 to contracted PPF powder from albumin as a result of the
settlement of a customer dispute as discussed further in the section titled, &#147;Management&#146;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of
Operations&#151;Matters Affecting Comparability&#151;Customer Settlement.&#148;&#160; This change in production mix resulted in
lower available quantities of albumin for sale during 2008.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our other product net
revenue increased $74.6&nbsp;million, or 36.5%, during the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008 as compared to the prior year. Our other product net revenue consists
primarily of revenue related to the Canadian blood system, where, in addition
to commercial sales of Gamunex, we have contract manufacturing contracts with
the two national Canadian blood system operators, CBS and Hema Quebec, as well
as sales of Koate&nbsp;DVI Factor&nbsp;VIII (human), hyperimmunes, intermediate
products, Thrombate&nbsp;III (human), and PPF powder, less SG&amp;A
reimbursements to certain international distributors.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our other product net
revenue includes $26.3&nbsp;million higher revenues during the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008 as compared to the prior year as a result of higher volumes of contracted
PPF powder in order to comply with contractual commitments associated with the
settlement of a customer dispute in 2007 as discussed previously. In addition,
we experienced improved pricing and volume of $7.8&nbsp;million and
$14.9&nbsp;million, respectively, related to intermediate products, such as
cryoprecipitate. Our other product net revenue was also favorably impacted by
increased Koate DVI Factor VIII (human) of $6.5&nbsp;million, resulting
primarily from improved pricing, and increased sales of Thrombate III (human)
of $5.5&nbsp;million. Finally, our other product net revenue benefited from
higher hyperimmune pricing of $16.4&nbsp;million, partially offset by lower
hyperimmune volumes of $7.0&nbsp;million. The increase in hyperimmune pricing
was primarily generated in the U.S. where we increased pricing during the
second quarter of 2008.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We increased prices for
substantially all of our products in most of our geographic regions as a result
of higher costs and demand. Our product net revenue was positively impacted by
$9.7&nbsp;million, or 0.8%, as a result of favorable foreign exchange rate fluctuations
in relation to the U.S. dollar during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 as
compared to the prior year. Prices in Canada are determined by contracts with CBS
and Hema Quebec. New five year contracts with increased pricing for contract
fractionation services and our commercial products, including Gamunex,
Plasbumin, and certain hyperimmune products took effect on April&nbsp;1, 2008.
Through the life of the Canadian contracts, prices escalate annually by inflation.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Cost of
Goods Sold and Gross Profit</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our gross profit was
$492.1&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 as compared to
$430.4&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007, representing
gross margin of 35.8% and 35.3%, respectively. Our gross profit is impacted by
the volume, pricing, and mix of our product net revenue as discussed above, as
well as the related cost of goods sold as discussed below. The net impact of
these items resulted in slightly higher gross margins during the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008 as compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our cost of goods sold
was $882.2&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 as compared
to $788.2&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007, representing
an increase of $94.0&nbsp;million, or 11.9%. The increase in our cost of goods
sold was driven primarily by higher unabsorbed TPR infrastructure and start-up
costs of $28.4&nbsp;million. Unabsorbed TPR infrastructure and start-up costs
amounted to $98.5&nbsp;million and $70.1&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2008 and 2007, respectively, representing approximately 7.2% and 5.8%,
respectively, of total net revenue. The higher unabsorbed TPR costs during 2008
resulted from the continued expansion of our plasma collection center platform
and the costs associated with our remediation efforts in certain centers
acquired from IBR as well as certain new centers opened by us. Until our plasma
collection centers reach normal operating capacity, we charge unabsorbed
overhead costs directly to cost of goods sold.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our cost of goods sold
for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 includes higher costs of production
of $52.3&nbsp;million, including foreign exchange, and higher costs associated
with an increase in volumes of $9.7&nbsp;million.&#160; The impact of foreign exchange in our cost of
production for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 is not material. During 2008, we
incurred non-capitalizable project and start-up costs of $26.0 million,
an increase of $4.7 million, as compared to the prior year, related to capital
projects. The
largest component of our cost of goods sold is the cost of source plasma which
represented in excess of 50% of our cost of goods sold in 2008 and 2007.&#160; The overall cost of source plasma is impacted
by the fully-loaded collection cost per liter of source plasma including donor
fees, labor, soft goods, facility costs, testing and unabsorbed TPR
infrastructure and start-up costs, the cost of plasma purchased from third-parties
and variability in protein yields, among other factors. Our internal cost per
liter of plasma, including unabsorbed TPR infrastructure and start-up costs,
increased by 7.7% during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, primarily
driven by higher unabsorbed infrastructure and start-up costs. Our
acquisition cost of plasma per liter of third party plasma increased 10.7%
during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 as compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007. Due to our long manufacturing cycle times, which range from 100&nbsp;days
to in excess of 400&nbsp;days, the cost of plasma is not expensed through cost
of goods sold until a significant period of time subsequent to its acquisition.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our inventory impairment
provisions, net, increased $2.0&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008 as compared to the prior year. Several of the more significant provisions
and recoveries impacting 2008 and 2007 are discussed further in the paragraphs

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the first and
second quarters of 2008, we incurred charges to cost of goods sold of
$16.3&nbsp;million and $7.0&nbsp;million, respectively, due to deviations from
our SOP&#146;s and cGMP at one of our plasma collection centers. As a result of
further investigations and new facts and circumstances, we subsequently
determined that certain impacted materials were saleable. We recorded
recoveries of $17.5&nbsp;million in 2008 directly to cost of goods sold as the
impacted material was converted to finished goods and sold to third
parties.&#160; We do not expect to recognize
significant further recoveries of the impacted material.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We settled a dispute with
a customer in September&nbsp;2007 regarding intermediate material manufactured
by us, which is used by this customer in its manufacturing process. We recorded
a charge to cost of good sold of $7.9&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007, which we recovered in its entirety during 2008 as the related materials
were determined to be saleable, converted into finished product, and sold to
other customers. During the first half of 2008, we recorded an additional
inventory impairment provision of $2.6&nbsp;million for products held in Europe
related to this dispute, for which we subsequently recovered $1.8&nbsp;million
during 2008 as the impacted material was determined to be saleable, converted
into finished product, and sold to other customers.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our inventory impairment
provisions, net, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007 were favorably
impacted by a $9.0&nbsp;million recovery from Bayer related to a Gamunex
production incident, which we recorded as a reduction of cost of goods sold
during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007. Other production issues during the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 resulted in higher inventory impairment
provisions of $3.0&nbsp;million as compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, we recorded an impairment charge of $3.6&nbsp;million primarily within cost
of goods sold related to capital lease assets and leasehold improvements at
certain of our plasma collection centers which were closed or were under
development and we no longer plan to open. During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2008, we also recorded a loss of $3.4&nbsp;million within cost of goods sold
related to two lease commitments associated with properties that we no longer
plan to operate as plasma collection centers. During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007, we recorded an impairment charge within cost of goods sold related to
equipment of $2.8&nbsp;million as a result of the discontinuation of a project.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During November&nbsp;2007,
we shut down portions of our Clayton, North Carolina facility consistent with
our cGMP operating practices for unplanned maintenance for approximately two
weeks. As a result of the unplanned plant maintenance, we recorded
$10.0&nbsp;million directly to cost of goods sold during the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007, which would normally have been capitalized to inventories.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additionally, our cost of
goods sold for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 reflects higher costs of
production due to the higher cost of raw materials, production volume
variances, and manufacturing mix and product yield variances, among other
items. Our cost of goods sold is impacted by our raw material costs, production
mix, cycle times, production capacities and normal production shut-downs, and
the release of finished product.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Operating Expense</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our SG&amp;A was
$227.5&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 as compared to
$189.4&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007, representing an
increase of $38.1&nbsp;million, or 20.1%. As a percentage of net revenue,
SG&amp;A was 16.6% and 15.5% for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 and
2007, respectively. Our SG&amp;A increased period over period as a result of
higher share-based compensation expense of $15.2&nbsp;million, costs of
$8.3&nbsp;million associated with the regulatory review process of our
terminated merger with CSL, which are unlikely to recur, merger related
retention expense (including fringe benefits) of $3.3&nbsp;million, unfavorable
foreign exchange impact of $6.7&nbsp;million resulting from a strengthening
U.S. dollar as compared to the euro pertaining </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">primarily to euro-denominated receivables, bad debt
expense of $4.2&nbsp;million related to outstanding notes receivables and
advances to one of our plasma suppliers due to uncertainty regarding collection,
and higher sales and marketing, information solutions, finance, human
resources, and business development expenses. These items were partially offset
by lower special recognition bonus expense of $1.5&nbsp;million, the absence of
legal fees of $5.7&nbsp;million associated with our litigation with Baxter
which was settled in 2007, and the absence of $15.3&nbsp;million of transition
and non-recurring expenses incurred in 2007 associated with the development of
our internal capabilities to operate as a standalone company apart from Bayer.
Additional information regarding the significant aforementioned items impacting
comparability between the periods presented is included in the section titled &#147;Management&#146;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#151;Matters
Affecting Comparability.&#148;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our R&amp;D was
$66.0&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 as compared to
$61.3&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007, representing an
increase of $4.7&nbsp;million, or 7.6%. As a percentage of net revenue, R&amp;D
was 4.8% and 5.0% for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 and 2007,
respectively. Research and development expenses are influenced by the timing of
in-process projects and the nature of expenses associated with these projects.
Our current research and development consists of a range of programs that aim
to obtain new therapeutic indications for existing products, enhance product
delivery, improve concentration and safety, and increase product yields. Our
R&amp;D increased period over period primarily as a result of $4.0&nbsp;million
in milestone payments made to Crucell under the terms of two exclusive
commercial license agreements entered into during 2008. Our R&amp;D expense was
negatively impacted by higher share-based compensation expense of
$1.0&nbsp;million and merger related retention expense (including fringe
benefits) of $0.6&nbsp;million during 2008 as compared to the prior year. Our
current R&amp;D activities continue to support Plasmin studies for aPAO and
ischemic stroke, Prolastin Alpha-1 aerosol studies, and the development of
Gamunex for subcutaneous administration.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Total
Other Non-Operating Expense, net</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The primary component of
our non-operating expense, net, is interest expense, net, which amounted to
$97.0&nbsp;million and $110.2&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2008 and 2007, respectively. Our weighted average interest rates on our outstanding
debt were 7.2% and 9.9% for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 and 2007,
respectively, which resulted in a lower cost of borrowing during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2008 as compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007,
despite higher average debt levels during 2008. The benefit of the lower cost
of borrowing during 2008 was partially mitigated by higher interest expense
related to our interest rate swaps of $12.0&nbsp;million as compared to 2007,
as a result of falling three-month LIBOR rates as compared to our fixed swap
rates. At December&nbsp;31, 2008, our interest rate swaps and caps hedged
approximately 56.4% of our total borrowings.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As discussed further in
the section titled, &#147;Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial
Condition and Results of Operations &#151;Matters Affecting Comparability,&#148; we
recorded other income of $12.9&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007 related to a litigation settlement with Baxter.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">(Provision)
Benefit for Income Taxes</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our income tax provision
was $36.6&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 as compared to
an income tax benefit of $40.8&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2007, resulting in effective income tax rates of 35.7% and (49.3)%,
respectively. Our effective income tax rates were different than the U.S.
statutory Federal income tax rate of 35% during each period due to the items
discussed in the following paragraphs.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We recognized a tax
benefit of $4.1&nbsp;million and $10.0&nbsp;million related to research and
development tax credits and $2.0&nbsp;million and $2.2&nbsp;million related to
qualified production activities during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2008
and 2007, respectively, and we recognized a tax benefit of $3.2&nbsp;million
during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007 related to the final settlement of
Bayer contingent consideration. These items were partially offset by state
income taxes (net of Federal benefit) of $4.1&nbsp;million and
$3.2&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 and 2007,
respectively.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We record a valuation
allowance to reduce our deferred tax assets to the amount that we believe is
more likely than not to be realized. In assessing the need for a valuation
allowance, we consider all available evidence, both positive and negative,
including historical levels of income, expectations and risks associated with
future taxable income, and ongoing prudent and feasible tax planning
strategies. As a result of our analysis of all available evidence, which
included ten consecutive quarters of cumulative pre-tax profits and our
expectations that we can generate sustainable consolidated taxable income for
the foreseeable future, we concluded during the third quarter of 2007 that it
was more likely than not that our deferred tax assets would be realized, and
consequently, we released the remaining valuation allowance related to our
deferred tax assets resulting in a $48.2&nbsp;million non-cash tax benefit.
During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2007, we also released a portion of our
valuation allowance equal to the amount of the current Federal income tax
provision.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31,
2008, our gross unrecognized tax benefits were approximately
$10.0&nbsp;million, of which approximately $7.1&nbsp;million would reduce our
effective income tax rate if recognized.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Net Income</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our net income was
$65.8&nbsp;million and $123.6&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2008 and 2007, respectively. The significant factors and events contributing to
the change in our net income are discussed above.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">LIQUIDITY
AND CAPITAL RESOURCES</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Cash

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, we generated cash from
operating activities of $234.2 million.&#160;
We received net proceeds from our IPO and the issuance of our 7.75%
Notes of $519.7 million and $583.9 million, respectively, which we used to
repay outstanding amounts under our First and Second Lien Term Loans (which
were terminated), repay outstanding amounts under our Revolving Credit
Facility, and to settle and terminate certain interest rate swap
contracts.&#160; Subsequently, we settled and
terminated our remaining interest rate swap contract.&#160; We invested $75.2 million and $30.4 million
in capital projects and the acquisition of twelve plasma collection centers
from IBR, respectively.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2009 and 2008, our cash and cash equivalents were
$65.2 million and $17.0 million, respectively.&#160;
We use our available cash balances to repay amounts outstanding under
our Revolving Credit Facility.&#160; We
deposit any excess cash amounts into an overnight investment account.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2009, we had $323.0
million of unused available borrowing capacity under our Revolving Credit
Facility.</font></p>

and debt financing, and through internally generated funds.&#160; Our borrowing facilities contain certain
default provisions and financial covenants as described below.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our operating assets (excluding the effects of business acquisitions),
net, (increased) decreased $(12.1) million, $(100.1) million, and $38.0 million
for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, 2008, and 2007, respectively, and
were driven by the following items.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our accounts receivable, net, decreased (increased)
$8.6 million, $(26.9) million, and $(9.2) million for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, 2008, and 2007, respectively.&#160;
Accounts receivable, net, balances are influenced by the timing of net
revenue and customer collections.&#160; Our
days sales outstanding (DSO) were 32 days, 34 days, and 35 days, for the years
ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, 2008, and 2007, respectively. Our international
sales terms generally range from 30 to 120 days due to industry and national
practices outside of the U.S., which can impact our DSO results. We calculate
DSO as our period end accounts receivable, net, divided by our prior three
months&#146; net sales, multiplied by 90 days.&#160;
Our calculation of DSO may not be consistent with similar calculations
performed by other companies.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our inventories (increased) decreased $(57.5) million,
$(92.9) million, and $26.8 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009,
2008, and 2007, respectively.&#160; Our
inventories fluctuate based upon our plasma collections, production mix and
cycle times, production capacities, normal production shut-downs, finished
product releases, targeted safety stock levels, and demand for our
products.&#160; Our biological manufacturing
processes result in relatively long inventory cycle times ranging from 100 days
to in excess of 400 days in addition to a required 60 day pre-production
holding period for plasma.&#160; Specialty
plasma, due to its nature, can often have cycle times in excess of one
year.&#160; Consequently, we have significant
investment in raw material and work-in-process inventories for extended
periods, and correspondingly, lower levels of finished goods inventories on
hand.&#160; The increase in our inventories
during 2009 was primarily driven by Thrombate III inventory build in
preparation of manufacturing transfer from Bayer, increased plasma collections
as compared to the prior year, and higher hyperimmune inventory levels.&#160; During 2008 and 2007, we repurchased
inventories with a value of approximately $28.6 million and $81.9 million,
respectively, from a Bayer affiliate in Germany, where we terminated our
distribution agreement.&#160; During November&nbsp;2007,
we experienced unplanned plant maintenance as discussed previously, which
resulted in lower inventory at December&nbsp;31, 2007, thus impacting the 2008
comparability.</font></p>

with IBR, we were required to prepay 90% for unlicensed plasma.&#160; Upon center licensure, we remit the remaining

$35.5 million, and $20.2 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009,
2008, and 2007, respectively.&#160; Our
liabilities fluctuate as a result of our cash management strategies and varying
due dates of accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other liabilities.&#160; The increase in our liabilities in 2009 was
primarily driven by higher accounts payable obligations of $16.1 million and
higher Medicaid, commercial rebates, and chargebacks of $14.2 million, partially
offset by lower interest payable and accrued goods and services.&#160; The increase in our liabilities in 2008 was
primarily driven by higher accounts payable obligations of $16.6 million,
higher accrued payroll, bonuses, and benefits of $13.7 million, higher
Medicaid, commercial rebates, and chargebacks of $2.2 million, and generally
higher liabilities for accrued goods, services, and other items, partially
offset by lower taxes payable of $10.6 million.&#160;
The increase in our liabilities in 2007 was primarily driven by higher
accounts payable obligations of $12.1 million, higher accrued payroll, bonuses,
and benefits of $12.5 million, higher Medicaid, commercial rebates, and
chargebacks of $5.5 million, higher interest payable of $11.8 million, higher
taxes payable of $9.8 million, partially offset by lower payables to related
parties of $27.3 million as a result of the termination of many of our then
existing transition services and distribution agreements with Bayer, and

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our capital expenditures were $75.2 million, $86.2 million, and $65.8
million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, 2008, and 2007,
respectively.&#160; Our capital expenditures
reflect investments in our facilities to support a platform for future growth
and efficiency improvements, including compliance enhancements, general
infrastructure upgrades, capacity expansions, and new facilities.&#160; Our capital expenditures also reflect
investments in our TPR infrastructure to support our plasma collection
efforts.&#160; Our capital expenditures for
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 reflect significantly lower spending
related to our TPR infrastructure as compared 2008 and 2007 as a result of the
maturation of our plasma collection platform, as well as the completion of
several projects.&#160; Our 2009 capital
expenditures include higher spending related to reliability/compliance
initiatives, as well as the initial investments in our new fractionation
strategic program.&#160; In addition,
significant investment which occurred in 2008 continued into 2009 for the new Thrombate
III purification facility, which is now mechanically complete.&#160; Two earlier investments, our Prolastin-C A1PI
facility and our Koate purification expansion Phase I project were approved by
the FDA during 2009.&#160; Additional
information regarding our currently planned capital programs is included in &#147;Management&#146;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of
Operations&#151;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#151;Sources of Credit, Access to Capital
and Cash Requirements, and Credit Ratings.&#148;</font></p>

outflows for the development of our plasma collection center platform,

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We completed our IPO on October&nbsp;6, 2009, which resulted in net

commissions.&#160; We used the net proceeds to
us from the IPO to repay $389.8 million and $129.9 million of principal under
our First and Second Lien Term Loans, respectively.&#160; We incurred legal and other costs related to
our IPO of approximately $3.9 million, of which $2.6 million is included as a
reduction of additional paid-in capital. On October&nbsp;21, 2009, we completed
a $600.0 million private placement of our 7.75% Notes at an issue price of
99.321% of par, which resulted in net proceeds to us of $583.9 million after
deducting underwriters&#146; commissions and the discount.&#160;&#160;&#160; We used a portion of the net proceeds to us
from the issuance of the 7.75% Notes to repay $290.9 million and $200.1 million
under our First and Second Lien Term Loans, respectively, and $55.6 million of
principal under our Revolving Credit Facility.&#160;
We incurred total debt issuance costs related to the issuance of the
7.75% Notes and the Revolving Credit Facility amendment of $14.9 million.&#160; During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009,
we made contractual principal payments of $5.3 million under our First Lien
Term Loan and during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 and 2007, we made
contractual principal payments of $7.0 million under our First Lien Term
Loan.&#160; Outstanding amounts under our
Revolving Credit Facility fluctuate based upon our business needs.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, we repurchased 251,108
shares of our common stock from employees for $4.2 million to settle their
withholding tax obligations.&#160; During the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009, we received proceeds from the exercise of
2,394,762 stock options of $7.6 million.&#160;
During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008, we repurchased 2,146,232
shares of our common stock from IBR for $33.5 million, plus accrued interest of
$1.9 million, and 69,648 shares of our common stock from employees for $0.7
million to settle their withholding tax obligations.&#160; During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009,
we recognized excess tax benefits related to share-based compensation of $13.4
million.</font></p>

7.75% Senior Unsecured Notes, due November&nbsp;15, 2016, at a price of 99.321%
of par, in a private placement to certain qualified institutional buyers.&#160; The 7.75% Notes yield 7.875% to maturity and
pay interest semi-annually on May&nbsp;15 and November&nbsp;15 to holders of
record on the immediately preceding May&nbsp;1 and November&nbsp;1,
respectively.&#160; The 7.75% Notes are
guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by our existing and future domestic
subsidiaries.&#160; Except as described below,
we will not be entitled to redeem the 7.75% Notes at our option prior to November&nbsp;12,
2012.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, at
any time during each twelve-month period ending on November&nbsp;15, 2010,
2011, and 2012, we may redeem up to 10% of the originally issued principal
amount of the 7.75% Notes at a redemption price of 103% of the principal amount
of the 7.75% Notes redeemed plus accrued and unpaid interest and additional
interest, if any, to the redemption date, subject to the rights of the holders
of the 7.75% Notes on the relevant record date to receive interest due on the
relevant interest payment date.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At any time, or from time to time, on or prior to November&nbsp;15,
2012, we may, at our option, redeem up to 35% of the aggregate principal amount
of the 7.75% Notes issued under the indenture with the net cash proceeds to us
of certain equity offerings at a redemption price equal to 107.75% of the
principal amount of the 7.75% Notes plus accrued and unpaid interest and
additional interest, if any, to the applicable redemption date, provided that
at least 65% of the aggregate principal amount of the 7.75% Notes originally
issued remains outstanding immediately after such redemption and the redemption
occurs within 90 days of the date of the closing of such equity offering.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the Make-Whole redemption feature, we may redeem 100% of the
principal plus a premium as defined under the indenture (computed using a
discount rate equal to the U.S. Treasury rate as of such redemption date plus
0.50%), plus accrued and unpaid interest and additional interest, if any, prior
to November&nbsp;15, 2012, with respect to some or all of the 7.75% Notes,
subject to the rights of the holders on the relevant record date to receive
interest due on the relevant interest payment date.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are not required to make mandatory redemption or sinking fund
payments with respect to the 7.75% Notes.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon a change of control, the 7.75% Notes are puttable at 101% of
principal plus accrued and unpaid interest and additional interest, if any.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We may incur additional indebtedness and our subsidiary guarantors may
also incur additional indebtedness if our Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio for our
most recently ended four full fiscal quarters immediately preceding the date on
which such additional indebtedness is incurred would have been at least 2.00 to
1.00, determined on a pro forma basis.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The indenture contains certain covenants limiting, subject to
exceptions, carve-outs and qualifications, our ability and our restricted
subsidiaries to: (i)&nbsp;sell assets; (ii)&nbsp;pay distributions on, redeem
or repurchase its capital stock or redeem or repurchase its subordinated debt; (iii)&nbsp;make
certain investments; (iv)&nbsp;incur or guarantee additional indebtedness or
issue preferred stock; (v)&nbsp;create or incur certain liens; (vi)&nbsp;enter
into agreements that restrict distributions or other payments from our
restricted subsidiaries to us; (vii)&nbsp;engage in certain sale and leaseback
transactions; (viii)&nbsp;engage in certain transactions with affiliates; (ix)&nbsp;transfer
or dispose of the capital stock of the restricted subsidiary to persons other
than us or our restricted subsidiaries; and (x)&nbsp;create unrestricted
subsidiaries.&#160; The indenture also
contains certain customary events of default.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with the sale of the 7.75% Notes, we and our subsidiaries
that guaranteed the 7.75% Notes entered into an exchange and registration
rights agreement with the initial purchasers of the 7.75% Notes on October&nbsp;21,
2009, pursuant to which we are obligated, by April&nbsp;19, 2010, to file with
Securities and Exchange Commission under the Securities Act of 1933, as
amended, a registration statement with respect to an offer to exchange the
7.75% Notes (and guarantees) for substantially identical new notes (and
guarantees) of ours.&#160; If we are not able
to effect this exchange offer, we have agreed to file a shelf registration
statement relating to re-sales of the 7.75% Notes. We will be obligated to pay
damages consisting of additional interest on the 7.75% Notes if, within the
periods specified in the Registration Rights Agreement, we do not file the
exchange offer registration statement or the shelf registration statement or we
do not comply with certain other obligations under the Registration Rights
Agreement.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Revolving
Credit Facility</font></u></i></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have a $325.0 million asset-based credit agreement administered by Wachovia
Bank, N.A., an affiliate of Wells Fargo Securities, which was amended on October&nbsp;15,
2009 as described below.&#160; We use our
available cash balances to repay amounts outstanding under this Revolving
Credit Facility.&#160; We deposit any excess
cash amounts into an overnight investment account.&#160; Outstanding principal under this facility is
due and payable on the maturity date of December&nbsp;6, 2011.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate based upon
either ABR or LIBOR, at our option, plus applicable margins based upon
borrowing availability.&#160; The ABR
represents the greater of the Federal Funds Effective Rate plus 0.50% or the
Prime Rate.&#160; Interest accrues on the
Revolving Credit Facility at the ABR plus 0.25-0.75% or LIBOR plus
1.50-2.00%.&#160; For the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2009, 2008, and 2007, the weighted average interest rates of our Revolving
Credit Facility were 2.79%, 4.79%, and 7.90%, respectively.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2008, the interest rates
on the ABR and LIBOR borrowings were 3.75% and 2.82%, respectively.&#160; No amounts were outstanding under the
Revolving Credit Facility at December&nbsp;31, 2009.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Revolving Credit Facility is secured by a Pledge and Security
Agreement dated December&nbsp;6, 2006 under which substantially all of our
personal property, including manufacturing equipment, accounts receivable,
inventory, and stock are pledged </font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;punctuation-wrap:simple;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of
